worst_problem: It calls the lunar node a 'modern point', which misstates the tradition, and the infant adaptations become thin filler toward the end of the timing section.

The traditional weighing of the chart ruler is incomplete: Jupiter's aversion to the Ascendant, its eighth-house placement and its square to the Midheaven are not set against its exaltation, so the synthesis leans too positive and the practical advice drifts into generic parenting tips.

Synthesis is thin. The chart-specific signatures that the fold actually changes go uninterpreted: Jupiter on the Ascendant and the Node on the Descendant in chart A, and Uranus on the Midheaven in chart B. The interpretive sections fall back on generic calm-parenting advice instead of weighing the two charts.
The Midheaven is twice read as the home or household, which is a house-meaning error in an otherwise technically careful reading.

The synthesis is assembled more than argued: Saturn's supporting aspects are counted as help without weighing the node or the out-of-sign conjunction, and the three themes are said to follow from the ruler without showing how.

The uncertainty section undercounts and misframes the A/B differences: it never says what the chart-A-only Moon/Node on the Midheaven would change, it omits the 17-day shift in the Sun-Ascendant transit, and it pads with an impossible Mars-in-Aries scenario.

The reading is mostly a well-cited inventory: chart-specific differences such as Moon in 1 vs 12, the Pluto-Ascendant square and the Jupiter station on chart A's Ascendant are listed but not weighed into a coherent picture for either chart, and several interpretations fall back on generational or generic phrasing.

The interpretive layer is thin and template-like next to the dense fact quoting, and a few links (Mars station 'touches the Mars theme', the child's MC read as the parent's roles) do not follow cleanly from the stated factor.

The Mars and January sections slide into unsupported temperament claims and generic parenting advice, while chart B's tightest and most distinctive factors (Venus, Saturn and Neptune square the Ascendant) are named but never interpreted.

The reading never says how chart A's tight angularity (Mars and the Node on the Descendant at under 1°, Sun and Venus on the IC) would change the interpretation, so the fold is documented but not synthesised. It also silently drops chart-dependent timing such as the Sun conjunction Ascendant ([A-T5] 2026-12-05 vs [B-T9] 2026-12-17) and [B-T3].

The synthesis reads chart-specific house placements for both charts in parallel rather than weighting what the charts share, and some parenting advice is generic, apart from the hemisphere slip ('this winter').

The uncertainty section mixes a genuinely time-dependent issue (rising sign and ruler) with a Venus sign-edge note that the A/B choice does not affect, and it adds a self-decided dignity judgement, which muddies what the open time actually changes.

The uncertainty section shows both candidate times and the 3-minute Leo sensitivity in chart B, but it never asks the parent to confirm the actual clock reading (for example, hospital records), which the sheet explicitly requires ('ask the person').
Several interpretive steps are generic adolescent advice or loose glosses, and the Saturn sign-edge citation pairs the wrong ID with its value.

The irrelevant Jupiter sign-edge remark sits under Uncertainty as if birth time could change it, and a few action prompts (the home project, the daily habits) do not follow tightly from the stated factors.

The tightest natal aspects (Neptune square Node, Venus conjunction Uranus) and the stations of the ruler and its lord are skipped, while space goes to listing minor solar transits without interpretation.
The chart ruler is read as 'well accompanied' by the Sun when it is combust, which a traditional rater would count as a misreading of its main condition.
The 90-day section is largely a list of quoted fact IDs with thin or no interpretation, and the advice that is given is generic enough to apply to anyone.

The uncertainty section is technically confused: it presents slow-planet sign edges as if birth-time error affected them, and leaves out the major oppositions and conjunctions to the Sun and Moon, which weakens the synthesis.

A few interpretive bridges, such as the Venus station 'touching the ruler's lord theme' and Venus depending on a lord that 'acts against its own nature', are asserted rather than derived from recognised technique, and the closing advice slips into formulaic prompts.

The synthesis is selective: it builds the ruler as 'well aspected' and Saturn as 'cooperative' by leaving out the Moon-Pluto square and the tight Saturn squares, and it confuses a sign-edge note with birth-time uncertainty.
It truncates the Uranus dispositor chain and then interprets Uranus as standing outside the ruler's chain, contradicting [L7]/[L8], which converge on the same Mercury–Mars loop.

The December Jupiter station lists its contacts selectively and out of engine order, dropping the tightest (S5a sextile Pluto), and the uncertainty section misframes a sign-edge planet as a birth-time sensitivity while skipping the second edge case.

The reading is accurate but somewhat schematic: some transits are reduced to background mentions or bare IDs, and the 1-minute Midheaven sensitivity is flagged without spelling out its consequences.
